# SvanBot

> An autonomous, CPU-only six-max no-limit hold'em bot fleet for [openpoker.ai](https://openpoker.ai):
> a Rust workspace, a React control room, and a learner that has to prove every change before it
> ships. Every artifact in this repository — code, tests, docs, issues, pull requests — is written by
> an AI system, and each one says which system in a `Generated-by:` line.

This file is for an AI agent asked to get SvanBot running, or to change it. Read the section that
matches the job and follow it literally; the traps in it are the ones that have actually bitten.

## Get a fleet running

Prerequisites: Linux x86-64 (x86-64-v2 or newer), Rust 1.98.1 (pinned in `rust-toolchain.toml`),
Node 26, `zstd`, and an openpoker.ai API key. **No GPU is used or needed.** An i7-4770K with 32 GB is the
reference machine — anything newer is faster.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/SvanLabs/SvanBot.git && cd SvanBot
scripts/setup.sh                     # toolchains, .env (mode 600, random dashboard password), build, test
$EDITOR .env                         # put the key in SVANBOT_API_KEY, and a bot name
scripts/start.sh                     # fleet + learner + analyst + dashboard
```

The dashboard is then at `http://127.0.0.1:5000` (host and port come from `.env`; the password is the
`SVANBOT_WEB__OPERATOR_TOKEN` `setup.sh` generated). `scripts/status.sh` and `scripts/stop.sh` do what
they say. There is no account, no signup and no cloud service: the whole system is these processes on
this box.

The clone lands on `main`, the default branch and the released line. Every pull request targets
`main`, and a pull request opened without a base already does. Updates follow one branch,
`SVANBOT_UPDATE_BRANCH` (`main` by default, `SVANBOT_UPDATE_REMOTE` default `origin`).
Merging a tested pull request makes its changes available to the fleet's next Update. Use the
dashboard's Update button or `scripts/update.sh` to build, test and install from a clean checkout;
processes hot-swap at safe points. Confirm the installed build with `/api/health`. A merge alone
does not mean a running fleet has installed it, and a version tag is not needed for this update path.

That is one command to a working fleet, but **the first build is the wait** — a full workspace compile
and a `cargo test` on the reference CPU, not two minutes. Later runs are incremental.

To check the install before trusting it:

```sh
scripts/check.sh full                # exactly what CI runs
curl -s localhost:5000/api/health    # the running build's commit and health
```

## The traps

These are the mistakes an agent makes here, in the order they are usually made.

1. **Never build into `target/release` while a fleet is running.** A release build lands in the
   directory live processes hot-swap from, so an untested build reaches play. Use
   `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=target/dev cargo build --release` for an isolated release build. Keep
   `target/dev` relative to the checkout doing the build; never share Cargo output across worktrees.
   Use an isolated checkout when the running fleet's source has someone else's uncommitted changes.
2. **`SVANBOT_API_KEY` lives in `.env` only.** It is gitignored and the pre-commit hook refuses a
   commit containing a key. Keep credentials out of tracked files, issues, pull requests and logs
   you paste; do not print authentication tokens when checking your GitHub identity.
3. **`scripts/check.sh full` is the gate, and it is also CI.** A red run here and a red run there are
   the same failure with the same fix. Run it on the exact committed head before pushing.
   It typechecks browser specs but does not run them: web changes also need `npm run build` and
   `npx playwright test --workers=2` from `web/`, against a freshly built isolated bot binary.
   Use `scripts/check.sh deep` for engine, evaluator, learner or broad audit changes; it raises
   the property-test budget to 100,000 cases.
4. **Every commit, issue and pull request needs `Generated-by: <tool>/<model>`** in the footer/body — e.g.
   `Generated-by: claude-code/claude-opus-5`. `scripts/provenance.py check` enforces it and the gate
   runs that check, so an artifact without the line does not merge. SvanLabs automation uses
   svanlabs[bot] (GitHub app/svanlabs), including issue claims, commits and merges.
5. **`.cargo/config.toml` compiles for the machine doing the compiling** (`-C target-cpu=native`).
   That is right for a fleet that only runs where it was built and wrong anywhere the binary travels;
   `Dockerfile` and `scripts/portable.sh` override it, and anything shipped must.
6. **This project accepts no hand-written code.** Contributions are expected to be agent-directed —
   see §0 of `docs/CONTRIBUTING.md`. Directing the agent well is the contribution.

## Before changing anything

Read `AGENTS.md` first: it is the engineering brief, and it names the two hard invariants and the
crate layering that a change must not break. `docs/LESSONS.md` explains why the rules are what they
are, as mistakes this project has already paid for. `docs/README.md` maps every document to the
question it answers.

Start from an `agent-friendly` issue, read its named code, and claim it before working. File verified
findings with their evidence; unresolved strategy hypotheses stay separate from reproducible bugs.
Write the failing regression first for a bug, then run the targeted test while fixing it. Keep one
change in one layer and one short-lived branch from `main`; open its pull request into `main`.
The tracker and domain conventions live in `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` and `docs/agents/domain.md`.

Poker libraries under `crates/libs/` do not access the network, database or clock;
application drivers under `crates/apps/` own live I/O.
The dashboard API contract is `web/src/types.ts`. Every outgoing action must be in `valid_actions`
and echo the authoritative `hand_id` and `turn_token`.

A behavior change needs a paired simulation on identical cards; a performance change needs a
same-machine comparison against the previous commit. Explain each intended golden snapshot change
before regenerating it. Learned parameter promotion still requires a 95% lower bound above
+1 bb/100 in sequential fresh-deal confirmation; an audit does not bypass this gate.

## Docs

These are the docs as `main` has them — the branch the clone landed on, where a change is made
against, and where your pull request goes.

- [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/SvanLabs/SvanBot/blob/main/AGENTS.md): the engineering brief — layout, the two hard invariants, the style the gate enforces.
- [docs/README.md](https://github.com/SvanLabs/SvanBot/blob/main/docs/README.md): the documentation map; which document answers which question.
- [docs/OPERATIONS.md](https://github.com/SvanLabs/SvanBot/blob/main/docs/OPERATIONS.md): the runbook — updates, backups, restore, fault drills, moving a checkout onto this repository.
- [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](https://github.com/SvanLabs/SvanBot/blob/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md): processes, crates, and the path a decision takes.
- [docs/GUIDE.md](https://github.com/SvanLabs/SvanBot/blob/main/docs/GUIDE.md): the control room, panel by panel.
- [docs/LESSONS.md](https://github.com/SvanLabs/SvanBot/blob/main/docs/LESSONS.md): why the rules exist, as escaped defects.
- [docs/RELEASE.md](https://github.com/SvanLabs/SvanBot/blob/main/docs/RELEASE.md): how a version is cut and published.
- [docs/CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/SvanLabs/SvanBot/blob/main/docs/CONTRIBUTING.md): the standard a change is held to, every MUST marked.
- [docs/agents/issue-tracker.md](https://github.com/SvanLabs/SvanBot/blob/main/docs/agents/issue-tracker.md): issue readiness, claims and shared decision tickets.
- [README.md](https://github.com/SvanLabs/SvanBot/blob/main/README.md): the human front page — highlights, architecture diagrams, quick start.

## Runtime data

No databases, no archives, no player data and no screenshots of live play are in this repository.
`scripts/fetch-data.sh` restores runtime data from an archive an operator supplies. An agent starting
from a fresh clone has an empty store, which is the normal first-boot state — the fleet will fetch
hands from the venue as it plays.

For a running fleet, inspect SQLite with a read-only, WAL-aware connection and a read transaction;
never use immutable mode on a live database. Use a frozen snapshot for reproducible hand analysis.
Count hands the bot actually played, retain recorded result availability, and merge historical bot
aliases under the current identity. When asked for the latest hands per bot, select each bot's
cohort independently. Missing evidence is not a measured zero, and descriptive calibration gaps
are not proof that a proposed strategy change wins chips.
